create_draft.description: Creates a draft with the DRAFT label. Give it content either with the plain to/subject/body fields (builds the RFC 2822/base64url encoding internally — use this for a normal draft) or with `message` (a raw Gmail Message resource with a hand-built `raw` blob — only needed for attachments, custom headers, or multipart bodies). If `message` is set, the plain fields below are ignored.

params.name: userId
params.description: The user's email address. Defaults to `me`, which refers to the authenticated user and is correct for almost every call — only override this if the token has delegated access to another mailbox.

params.name: message
params.description: The message content of the draft (object (Message)) as a raw Gmail Message resource — must include a base64url-encoded `raw` RFC 2822 blob. Only needed for attachments, custom headers, or multipart bodies; for a normal draft use the plain to/subject/body fields below instead and leave this unset.

params.name: to
params.description: Comma-separated recipient email address(es). Ignored if `message` is set.

params.name: subject
params.description: The draft's subject line. Ignored if `message` is set.

params.name: body
params.description: The draft's body text. Ignored if `message` is set.

params.name: cc
params.description: Comma-separated Cc recipient email address(es). Ignored if `message` is set.

params.name: bcc
params.description: Comma-separated Bcc recipient email address(es). Ignored if `message` is set.

params.name: html
params.description: If true, `body` is treated as HTML instead of plain text. Ignored if `message` is set.

send_message.description: Sends the specified message to the recipients in the To, Cc, and Bcc headers. Requires a hand-built, base64url-encoded RFC 2822 `raw` blob — for a plain email or reply, use send_email or reply_to_message instead; reach for this tool only when you need something those can't express (attachments, custom headers, multipart bodies).

params.name: userId
params.description: The user's email address. Defaults to `me`, which refers to the authenticated user and is correct for almost every call — only override this if the token has delegated access to another mailbox.

params.name: raw
params.description: The entire RFC 2822 message (headers + body, with `To`/`Cc`/`Bcc`/`Subject` etc. as headers), base64url-encoded — this is how a full email is supplied for sending. Not explicitly marked required by the provider docs.

send_email.description: Sends a plain email from ordinary fields (to, subject, body) — builds the RFC 2822 message and base64url encoding internally, so you never hand-construct or encode it yourself. For attachments, custom headers, or multipart bodies, use send_message with a hand-built `raw` instead. Not a distinct upstream endpoint — a server-side wrapper around the same messages.send call as send_message.

params.name: userId
params.description: The user's email address. Defaults to `me`, which refers to the authenticated user and is correct for almost every call — only override this if the token has delegated access to another mailbox.

params.name: to
params.description: Comma-separated recipient email address(es) for the To header.

params.name: subject
params.description: The email subject line.

params.name: body
params.description: The email body text.

params.name: cc
params.description: Comma-separated Cc recipient email address(es).

params.name: bcc
params.description: Comma-separated Bcc recipient email address(es).

params.name: html
params.description: If true, `body` is sent as HTML instead of plain text.

reply_to_message.description: Replies to an existing message with plain body text — looks up the original message to set the Subject, recipient, and threading headers (In-Reply-To, References) automatically, and builds the RFC 2822/base64url encoding internally, so you never hand-construct or encode it yourself. For attachments, custom headers, or multipart bodies, use send_message with a hand-built `raw` instead. Not a distinct upstream endpoint — a server-side wrapper around messages.get (to read threading headers) plus the same messages.send call as send_message.

params.name: message_id

params.description: The reply body text.

params.name: bcc
params.description: Comma-separated Bcc recipient email address(es).

params.name: html
params.description: If true, `body` is sent as HTML instead of plain text.

response_fields.name: startTime
response_fields.description: Optional start time for auto-replies (epoch ms). Replies only to messages received after this time. Must precede endTime if both are set.

response_fields.name: endTime
response_fields.description: Optional end time for auto-replies (epoch ms). Replies only to messages received before this time. Must follow startTime if both are set.

create_filter.description: Creates a mail filter (an account can have a maximum of 1,000 filters).

params.name: userId
params.description: The user's email address. Defaults to `me`, which refers to the authenticated user and is correct for almost every call — only override this if the token has delegated access to another mailbox.

params.name: id
params.description: The server-assigned filter ID (omit when creating).

params.name: criteria
params.description: Matching criteria for the filter.

params.name: criteria.from
params.description: Sender's display name or email address.

params.name: criteria.to
params.description: Recipient's display name or email address (matches To/Cc/Bcc). Local part alone works case-insensitively, e.g. `example` matches `example@gmail.com`.

params.name: criteria.subject
params.description: Case-insensitive phrase in the subject; whitespace trimmed/collapsed.

params.name: criteria.query
params.description: Only match messages matching this query, in Gmail search-box syntax.

params.name: criteria.negatedQuery
params.description: Only match messages NOT matching this query, same syntax.

params.name: criteria.hasAttachment
params.description: Whether the message has any attachment.

params.name: criteria.excludeChats
params.description: Whether to exclude chats from the match.

params.name: criteria.size
params.description: Size of the entire RFC822 message in bytes (headers + attachments), compared per sizeComparison.

params.name: criteria.sizeComparison
params.description: How `size` should relate to the actual message size.

params.name: action
params.description: Action the filter performs when criteria match.

params.name: action.addLabelIds[]
params.description: Labels to add to matching messages. System labels use fixed well-known strings (INBOX, UNREAD, SPAM, TRASH, IMPORTANT, STARRED, DRAFT, SENT, CATEGORY_PERSONAL, CATEGORY_SOCIAL, CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS, CATEGORY_UPDATES, CATEGORY_FORUMS). User-created labels use opaque IDs like `Label_8927364` — call list_labels first to resolve the correct ID; never guess or invent one.

params.name: action.removeLabelIds[]
params.description: Labels to remove from matching messages. System labels use fixed well-known strings (INBOX, UNREAD, SPAM, TRASH, IMPORTANT, STARRED, DRAFT, SENT, CATEGORY_PERSONAL, CATEGORY_SOCIAL, CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS, CATEGORY_UPDATES, CATEGORY_FORUMS). User-created labels use opaque IDs like `Label_8927364` — call list_labels first to resolve the correct ID; never guess or invent one.

params.name: action.forward
params.description: Email address to forward matching messages to, keeping the original sender in From.

response_fields.name: sendAsEmail
response_fields.description: The address that appears in the From: header for mail sent with this alias. Read-only except on create.

response_fields.name: displayName
response_fields.description: Name shown in the From: header. For custom aliases, empty means Gmail uses the primary address's name. If the admin disabled name-format changes, updates to the primary login's name silently fail.

response_fields.name: replyToAddress
response_fields.description: Optional Reply-To: address. Empty means no Reply-To: header is generated.

response_fields.name: signature
response_fields.description: Optional HTML signature added to new messages composed with this alias in the Gmail web UI (not added to already-composed mail).

response_fields.name: isPrimary
response_fields.description: Read-only. Whether this is the account's primary login address — exactly one exists and it can't be removed from the send-as collection.

response_fields.name: isDefault
response_fields.description: Whether this is the default From: address for new messages/vacation replies. Exactly one address may be true; setting one to true flips the previous default to false.

response_fields.name: treatAsAlias
response_fields.description: Whether Gmail should treat this address as an alias of the primary address. Custom "from" aliases only.

response_fields.name: smtpMsa
response_fields.description: Optional outbound SMTP relay for mail sent with this alias. Empty means Gmail sends directly. Custom aliases only.

response_fields.name: smtpMsa.host
response_fields.description: SMTP service hostname.

response_fields.name: smtpMsa.port
response_fields.description: SMTP service port.

response_fields.name: smtpMsa.username
response_fields.description: Write-only — used for create/update, never returned in responses.

response_fields.name: smtpMsa.password
response_fields.description: Write-only — used for create/update, never returned in responses.

response_fields.name: smtpMsa.securityMode
response_fields.description: Protocol securing the SMTP connection. `none` is unsecured and requires port 25.

response_fields.name: verificationStatus
response_fields.description: Read-only. Whether the address is verified for use as a send-as alias. Custom aliases only.
